page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the page number and running head at the top. No margin notes or footnotes. At the right edge a strip of the facing page shows, which is the neighbouring page's edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: sanæ[?] mentis negaverit : ut falutem populi, id eft, fubditorum exclufo Rege, fupremam effe Legem quis dixerit, nifi aut Fatuus, aut Impostor ? Fatuus, fi ipfi fibi fic dicenti fidem habeat ; fi non habet, Impostor. Sed enim quifquis ipfius Aphorifmi vi-ginem attentius infpexerit, lubentius conceffurum arbitror, de falute Principis præcise intelligi debere, quàm de falute Subditorum præcise. Scilicet Romanis ad nos devenit celebre hoc dictum, illis tunc ufurpatum, cùm maximè floreret Respublica fub statu populari. Non eft autem quod quis mire[?]tur, fuiffe illis falutem populi fupremam Legem, quibus ipse Populus erat suprema Potestas. Erat ergo prudentium illorum veterum, qui Aphorismi hujus primi authores extiterunt, judicio, supremæ potestatis falus suprema Lex ; Populi nimirum in Democratiâ, aut in Monarchiâ Principis.

XVIII. Dico fecundò ; dato non concefso, Aphorifmum hunc de Populi, i. e. fubditorum falute prò-prie intelligi ; adhuc tamen, perversè detorquent in Regiæ dignitatis præjudicium, qui vel sic po-testatem[?] ejus ampliorem reddit & illustriorem. Hoc sensu scilicet, Regem qui populo Leges & Jus dedit, non ita se voluisse Legum vinculis astringi, ut non liceret ipsi, ubi Reipublicæ falus palàm peri-clitaretur[?], regni populiqué sibi à Deo commissi saluti consulere, etiam contra verba Legis. Non quòd liceat subditis, tuendæ libertatis obtentu, Legum & omnia fidelitatis vincula abrumpere, & Regiam authoritatem intolerando fastu sub pedibus conculcare. Sed quòd Principi liceat, tuendæ subditorumque salutis causâ, strictam Legum observantiam ad tempus seponere, & arbitrario juri aliquantisper uti ; ne ex nimium superstitiosâ & intempestivâ Legum reverentiâ, sëque & subditum sibi populum, ipsasque etiam Leges, in hostium potestatem devenire patiatur.

page.notes: The last line, "XIX. Dic", is cut off at the right by the edge of the facing page, so the rest of the line is not visible. "sanæ" at the start of the page: the first letter is doubtful and may be "s" (long s printed like f). "mirctur" is probably "miretur", printed as "mirctur"; I have marked the doubtful letter. "vi-ginem" is split at a line end with a printed hyphen; the first part "vi" is doubtful. "po-testatem" and "peri-clitaretur" at line ends are partly doubtful. Italics are judged from the scan and may be incomplete. The running head is set in italic in the original for the words Legum, Humanarum, causa and Finali; the running head is given as plain text.
